title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Mars
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Mars, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his fire and his knife. Mars is the planet of the knife and the forge: surgery, bloodletting, the taming of wild beasts, the smithy's fire, war, and banditry fall under him, with army camps, battlefields, and places of judgment among his locations. His seat in the body is the gallbladder, the source of yellow bile and heat, and bright red is his color. A waxing Moon facing him by aspect is counted a misfortune; his is the figure the lunar doctrine watches hardest.
